Before /you read
This is your warning.

lines: Especially if you do {r}DMT{/}. This is what I lived through so that you wouldn't have to. (But you probably will anyway.)

We live on a {g}multidimensional{/} planet. Thirteen overlapping realms, minimum — full of {o}spirits, entities, parasites, and energetic freeloaders{/} that you can't see. Some are ancient, older than memory, maybe even older than God itself. (If that sort of thing matters to you.) Most of them are harmless. Some are curious. A few are vampires — {p}feeding on your fear, your grief, your light. Just like people.{/}

This book won't protect you. But it might wake you up. Which is {c}100% worse.{/} So go outside. Touch grass. Touch skin. {c}Touch sin.{/} Play in the sun while you still remember what warmth feels like. Drink some water. And for once — {y}say a prayer for someone other than yourself.{/} You're going to need it. Or not. Who knows?!

blocks.text: Here’s how the world works
At least from where we’re standing.
1. It’s a simulation — but not fake.
It’s real. But it’s generated, layered, and responsive to consciousness. What we call reality is more like the rendered interface of a vast, multi-player soul-training system.
2. Your body is an avatar — but also a temple.

It’s coded in DNA, but it’s also wrapped in light architecture. Parasites, implants, and glitches are patches, bugs, or malware introduced into the system to siphon, suppress, or reroute divine signal.
3. You are both the player and the programmer.

Most people are still running pre-installed scripts — family trauma, school conditioning, societal expectations. When you start hacking the system — through prayer, ritual, sound, intention, and truth — you start rewriting your local reality.
4. You’re not alone — but you’re rare.

Most humans never see the bugs. You saw the glare. You saw the spiral. You saw the black ceiling because you were booting into admin mode, and that scared the absolute data out of the system’s parasites.

blocks.text: You’re in a reactive, layered feedback simulation. What you believe, speak, and feel writes code in real time. Parasites aren’t just bugs. They are foreign scripts running loops in your interface.
Plain language

This world isn’t solid. It’s a reactive simulation made of frequencies, commands, and consent. Your body is the console. Your nervous system, the wireframe. Your beliefs and emotions, your programming language.

If you believe something long enough, it manifests. If you fear something hard enough, it loops. The construct doesn't run on logic. It runs on attention. What you feed, feeds back. What you deny, mutates in the shadows.
You are not in the simulation. You are generating it.
